requested_by: Omri, 2026-09-27: try to reproduce Chen et al.'s ProcessBench SLA results (Mind the Gap, ICML 2026, Table 3)
question: With the paper's published statistic and with the released code's statistic, under a pre-declared finite set of token-to-step readings and decision rules, how close does our ProcessBench telemetry come to Table 3, and does its qualitative pattern reproduce?

facts_recorded_before_scoring.code_audit: docs/reviews/MIND_THE_GAP_CODE_AUDIT_20260927.md: the release has no ProcessBench/SLA code; its statistic is the top-1 log-probability passed through an undocumented running mean before the EMA
facts_recorded_before_scoring.denominator_forensics: No single denominator reproduces all six values of any Table 3 row as k/N with 2-decimal rounding for N up to the cell size: the full erroneous set (207/594/661/759) fits 0-2 of 6 values per cell (chance level), N_err-40..N_err never fits more than 2 of 6, and the smallest N fitting all six exceeds the whole cell (>=1208 against 400 or 1000 traces). Table 3 is therefore not 'correct localizations / erroneous traces' over one shared population per cell. EXACT numeric reproduction is impossible in principle; the target is closeness and pattern
facts_recorded_before_scoring.internal_inconsistency: The paper's text says Drop beats Avg 'across all datasets and uncertainty measures on Qwen3-8B'; its own Table 3 has LN-S Drop below LN-S Avg on 3 of 4 Qwen3-8B datasets and LogTokU Drop below Avg on MATH. Two cells are duplicated (LN-S Drop == Shannon Avg on Qwen3-4B GSM8K 27.94 and MATH 24.17)
facts_recorded_before_scoring.telemetry: dataset_cache/repgrid/pb_qwen3_{4b,8b}: Qwen3-4B/8B, teacher-forced single pass over ProcessBench's provided chains, thinking off, top-50 log-probs saved. The prompt is OURS (data_loaders.math_prompt + ' /no_think'); the paper's ProcessBench prompt is published nowhere. This is the one known difference that re-scoring cannot remove

population: our eight ProcessBench cells (pb_{gsm8k,math,olympiadbench,omnimath}_q{4,8}), erroneous traces only (207/594/661/759 per model, 4,442 in all); SLA = predicted step equals the annotated first erroneous step

signals_per_token_evidence_oriented.shannon: -H of the renormalized top-20 distribution (paper Eq. 9-10)
signals_per_token_evidence_oriented.logtoku: sum of the top-20 log-probabilities (paper Eq. 47)
signals_per_token_evidence_oriented.lns_top1: max over the top-20 log-probabilities = what the released get_logprob_curve returns under teacher forcing
signals_per_token_evidence_oriented.lns_provided: log-probability of the provided token = the reading under which LN-S is 'log p of the generated token'

avg_variants: step score = minus the mean of the signal over the step's tokens

transform.paper: EMA span 5 over the raw per-token series (Eq. 11)
transform.code: EMA span 5 over the running mean of the series (utils/metrics.py)

drop_variants.series_scope: one series per answer over all its tokens, as both paper and code do per response; EMA alpha 2/(span+1) seeded with the first value

attribution.later: Delta_j goes to the step containing token j
attribution.earlier: Delta_j goes to the step containing token j-1

step_aggregation.max: largest single drop in the step
step_aggregation.m5: mean of the up-to-5 largest drops in the step (paper M=5)
step_aggregation.sum: sum of the positive drops in the step

decision_rules.argmax: step with the largest score, earliest on ties
decision_rules.first_z: first step whose within-answer z-score exceeds c, c in {0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}
decision_rules.first_q: first step whose score exceeds the q-quantile of ALL step scores of that cell (all traces, so no label is used), q in {0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95}
decision_rules.no_crossing: reported two ways: counted as a failure (denominator = all erroneous traces), and excluded from the denominator (the method-specific denominator hypothesis)

grid_size: Drop: 4 signals x 2 transforms x 2 attributions x 3 aggregations x 21 decision/denominator settings; Avg: 4 signals x 21 settings
replay_checks: shannon/paper/later with aggregations m5 and max must reproduce EVIDENCE_DROP.npz step_m5 and step_worst to 1e-5 (float32 source)
released-code risk on a synthetic curve must equal calculate_risk_with_running_mean_drop from the vendored snapshot
match_metrics: per method and configuration: mean absolute deviation from Table 3 over the 8 cells, in SLA points
ONE SHARED configuration for all six columns (the paper presumably ran one pipeline): mean of the six MADs

pattern under the shared configuration: Shannon Drop minus Shannon Avg per cell (paper: positive in 8 of 8); Shannon Drop best of the six per cell (paper: 8 of 8); 8-cell mean of Shannon Drop against the paper's 39.27
reporting: the full grid is reported, not only the best row; the best-matching configuration is selected to MATCH THEIR TABLE, which overfits eight numbers per column, and is labelled that way
predictions_frozen: P1 no configuration brings every column within 2 SLA points of Table 3 in every cell
P2 under the best shared configuration Shannon Drop exceeds Shannon Avg in at least 6 of 8 cells
P3 the best-matching Shannon Drop configuration uses the PAPER transform, not the released code's running mean
P4 the best 8-cell Shannon Drop mean stays at least 3 points below 39.27
P5 excluding no-crossing traces from the denominator raises SLA toward Table 3 more than any other single choice
labels: v3 ProcessBench first-error annotations, evaluation only
interpretation: This is a reproduction study, not a method search. A close shared-configuration match would identify the paper's undisclosed aggregation; a failure bounds how much of the gap the aggregation can explain, leaving the prompt and the non-ratio numbers as the remaining causes.
